place.en: Black Pine Ridge · the sky turns

setup.zh: 鸟忽然全停了，风里一股铁锈味，山梁上的云往下压。蹄印还新，鹿就在前面。
setup.en: The birds stop all at once; the wind smells of rust; cloud presses down over the ridge. The tracks are fresh, the deer just ahead.

recap.zh: 天变了。暴雨里，爹的膝盖在崖边软了；你把他拽进山壁，自己被甩下了崖。
recap.en: The sky turned. In the storm Father's knee gave at the cliff edge; you hauled him against the rock and were thrown over yourself.

zh: 鸟不叫了。风里有铁锈的味道。
en: The birds have stopped. The wind smells of rust.
Over the ridge, the clouds are coming down.

story.zh:
是你先觉出不对的。

鸟不叫了——不是黑松岭那种一直没有的静，是刚才还有几声，忽然全停了。风里有一股味道，像铁锈，又像雷雨前翻起来的土腥。你抬头，树梢一动不动，可天边那道山梁上的云，正在往下压。

「爹，」你拉住他，「第三条。」

你爹也看见了。他看了看天，又看了看前面——蹄印还新，鹿就在前面，也许再走半里地就能看见。
story.en:
You are the first to feel something wrong.

The birds have stopped — not the silence Black Pine Ridge always keeps, but a few calls a moment ago and now, all at once, none. There is a smell on the wind like rust, like the earth turned up before a thunderstorm. You look up: the treetops are perfectly still, but over the far ridge the clouds are pressing down.

"Father," you say, catching his arm. "The third rule."

Your father has seen it too. He looks at the sky, and then ahead — the tracks are fresh, the deer is right there in front of you; half a li more and you might see it.

label.en: The third rule: turn and run

exits.means: turns back at once as the rule says, runs for the marks

story.zh:
他咬了咬牙。

然后他转过身：「走。」

你们往回跑。你认着记号，一道一道往回数：四十一，四十，三十九——

天是突然塌下来的。前一刻，还有一线光从树缝里漏下来；后一刻，林子里就黑了，黑得像有人一把扯过一块黑布，把天蒙住了。风从山顶灌下来，满山的黑松一齐弯了腰，呜呜地响，像是整座山在哭。

雨砸下来了。

不是下，是砸。雨点有黄豆那么大，打在脸上生疼。眨眼之间，山路成了河，泥水裹着碎石往下冲。你看不清三步以外的东西，只看得见你爹一瘸一拐的背影在雨幕里晃。

第二十七道记号那里，是一段贴着山崖的窄坡。

你爹的左膝，在这里软了一下。

他整个人往崖外一歪。你想都没想——不，你想了，你想得飞快：你离他两步，坡外是崖，你拉他，你们俩可能一起下去；你不拉，他一定下去。

你扑过去，一把抓住他的腰带，把他往里一拽，拽得他撞在了山壁上。

你自己，被那股劲甩了出去。

你爹回过身来，伸手来抓。他的手指擦过你的手腕——

没抓住。
story.en:
He sets his jaw.

Then he turns round. "Go."

You run back. You read the marks and count them down, one by one: forty-one, forty, thirty-nine —

The sky falls all at once. One moment a thread of light still leaks between the trees; the next the woods are black, as if someone had snatched up a black cloth and thrown it over the sky. Wind pours down off the peak, every black pine on the mountain bends double, moaning, as if the whole mountain were weeping.

The rain comes down like stones.

Not falling — hurled. Drops the size of beans that sting your face. In the blink of an eye the path is a river, mud and gravel pouring down it. You can't see three steps ahead; you can see only your father's limping back swaying in the curtain of rain.

At the twenty-seventh mark the path is a narrow slope hugging the cliff.

There, your father's left knee gives.

His whole body tips toward the drop. You don't even think — no, you do think, and fast: you are two steps from him, the slope ends at a cliff; pull him, and you may both go over; don't pull him, and he goes over for certain.

You throw yourself at him, grab his belt and haul him inward, so hard he slams into the rock face.

And you yourself are flung out by the same force.

Your father twists round and reaches for you. His fingers brush your wrist —

and miss.

exits.means: keeps chasing the deer a little further before turning back

story.zh:
你爹咬了咬牙：「半里。就半里。」

你们又追了半里。林子深处，一截鹿角在树后一闪——然后，天就塌下来了。

前一刻，还有一线光从树缝里漏下来；后一刻，林子里就黑了。风从山顶灌下来，满山的黑松一齐弯了腰。雨砸下来，山路成了河。多追的那半里，现在要一步一步在泥水里还回去。你认着记号往回数，数得比去时慢得多。

第二十七道记号那里，是一段贴着山崖的窄坡。你爹的左膝，在这里软了一下。

你扑过去，一把抓住他的腰带，把他往里一拽，拽得他撞在了山壁上。

你自己，被那股劲甩了出去。你爹的手指擦过你的手腕——没抓住。你往下滚的时候，撞上的石头，比该撞的多。
story.en:
Your father sets his jaw. "Half a li. Just half a li."

You follow the tracks half a li further. Deep among the trees an antler flashes behind a trunk — and then the sky falls.

One moment a thread of light still leaks between the trees; the next the woods are black. Wind pours off the peak and every pine bends double. The rain comes down like stones and the path becomes a river. The extra half li must now be paid back step by step through the mud. You count the marks down, far slower than you counted them up.

At the twenty-seventh mark the path is a narrow slope hugging the cliff. There, your father's left knee gives.

You throw yourself at him, grab his belt and haul him inward, so hard he slams into the rock.

And you are flung out by the same force. His fingers brush your wrist — and miss. On the way down you hit more rocks than you should have.
